VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a mildly-to-moderately attractive case anchored by improving fundamental trajectory and reasonable valuation, partially offset by structural headwinds. On Pillar 1 (fundamentals/trajectory): Q1 2026 showed revenue +2.9% YoY to $34.4B, adjusted EPS of $1.28 beating consensus, record adjusted EBITDA of $13.4B, and the first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds in 13 years (55K). Management raised adjusted EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99 and guided FCF of $21.5B+. The company is executing a transformation under new CEO Dan Schulman with $5B in planned OpEx savings, AI-driven cost reductions (85% of network issues autonomously resolved), and disciplined capital allocation including $5.4B returned to shareholders in Q1 alone. However, the business remains in a saturated U.S. wireless market with flat wireless service revenue growth expected for 2026, trailing 5-year earnings declining ~6%/year, and net margins slipping from 13% to 12.4%. The Frontier acquisition adds fiber growth optionality but ~30M homes but increased leverage to 2.6x net debt/EBITDA. The 6% yield and 6.1% attractive for On Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): Q1 2026 earnings just reported on April 27 with beats on EPS and subscriber metrics; management raised guidance, signaling confidence. The stock rallied 20.6% over the prior quarter, but the positive earnings event and guidance raise provide a near-term fundamental re-rating anchor. Multiple analysts have raised price targets. The combination of a credible turnaround narrative, dividend yield ~6%, and improving execution supports a modestly positive view, though structural market saturation and heavy debt load cap the upside.
